items.title: export.spec.ts:177 flake — indexOf('1.0') false-matches INDEX.md generation timestamp
items.status: confirmed-root-cause, fix sketch verified complete, packet defined

evidence: export.spec.ts:175-177 — `const highIdx = content.indexOf('9.0'); const lowIdx = content.indexOf('1.0'); expect(highIdx).toBeLessThan(lowIdx);` on the per-topic INDEX.md content
export.ts:395 — per-topic INDEX.md header `<!-- generated by sox-memory export at ${genTimestamp} -->` is written ABOVE the table rows
export.ts:376 — `genTimestamp = nowIso()`; export.ts:83-85 — `nowIso()` is `new Date().toISOString()`

A toISOString() value like `2026-08-08T19:51:01.012Z` contains the substring "1.0" inside "51.01" (seconds ending in 1 AND ms in 000-099 → P = 6/60 × 100/1000 = 1.0% of clock states; task cites ~1.6% observed — same mechanism)
When the header contains "1.0", indexOf('1.0') resolves to the header (top of file) instead of the low-importance row, so lowIdx < highIdx and the assertion fails — the flake

Flake hit LIVE during the deploy's memory-core suite — deploy report deviation B: '1 test failure in export.spec.ts (writes per-topic INDEX.md...) Debugger confirmed pre-existing flaky assertion (indexOf('1.0') false-matched timestamp). Not a regression.'
unverified: Exact observed failure rate (~1.6% per task vs ~1.0% computed from the clock-state distribution) — same mechanism, cosmetic discrepancy
BL-202's current status in the backlog graph — unreadable this session because the backlog CLI is broken (see item TURSO-DRIVER-072)

functions: test 'writes per-topic INDEX.md listing nodes sorted by importance' (export.spec.ts:152-184) — replace the indexOf assertions
spec file imports (line 12) — add `vi` to the vitest import
fixSurface.shape: Assert on parsed table rows instead of whole-file indexOf: filter content lines matching the table-row shape (`/^\| /` excluding the `|-------|` separator), locate the row whose importance column equals '9.0' and the row whose importance column equals '1.0', assert rowIndex(9.0) < rowIndex(1.0). Freeze the clock with `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['Date'] })` + `vi.setSystemTime(new Date('2026-08-08T19:51:01.012Z'))` (a timestamp containing "1.0") before exportMarkdown, restore with afterEach useRealTimers. NO change to export.ts — zero behavior change. write.ts uses the same Date clock (write.ts:329) so t_created is deterministic under the frozen clock; both rows share t_created, harmless because the sort is importance-first.

dependencies.ordering: Standalone — touches only export.spec.ts; may ride with any other packet that does not touch export.spec.ts, but standalone is cleanest.

testPlan.name: per-topic INDEX.md sorts by importance — row-parsed, deterministic under frozen clock (BL-202 regression)
testPlan.assertion: Under `vi.setSystemTime('2026-08-08T19:51:01.012Z')` with toFake:['Date']: (RED leg) the OLD assertion `expect(highIdx).toBeLessThan(lowIdx)` must FAIL deterministically (header '1.0' beats the row); (GREEN leg) the row-parsed assertion (9.0-row before 1.0-row) must PASS. Also must PASS with the real clock (header-independent by construction).
testPlan.whyCatches: The old assertion is clock-sensitive: it fails exactly when the header timestamp embeds "1.0". The frozen clock makes that failure deterministic (red), and the row-parse makes the assertion clock-independent (green) — BL-225 demands both observed.

packet.recommendation: Standalone micro-packet: single-file test-only change in export.spec.ts. Executor demonstrates red (old assertion + frozen clock) then green (row-parse) per BL-225, runs `npx nx test memory-core` for the export.spec.ts suite, commits by explicit pathspec.
packet.risk: LOW — no production code touched; fake timers scoped to toFake:['Date'] to avoid disturbing any setTimeout-based paths

items.title: @tursodatabase/database-common@0.7.2 regression: rejects CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS on existing index + FK references during UPDATE node — backlog CLI is down
items.status: confirmed-root-cause (driver regression, not adapter code); workspace immune; fix surface + packet defined

evidence: LIVE REPRO: `backlog list-items --filter '{}'` and even `backlog version` crash: `Parse error: index "node_uid_unique" already exists` at database-common/dist/promise.js:470 → @adhd/sox-store-adapter/dist/turso-adapter.js:393 (TursoAdapterImpl.exec) → @adhd/sox-graph-store/dist/index.js:689 (SqliteGraphBackend.applySchema). Every one-shot CLI process re-runs applySchema on connect (schemaApplied flag guards per-process only), so once the index exists every connect crashes.

The DDL in question: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "node_uid_unique"` / `ix_edge_unique` — in workspace source at libs/data/graph/graph-store/src/index.ts:119,224,254, executed on every store open via memory-core schema.ts:90 (DDL_BASE = GRAPH_DDL + MEMORY_ONLY_DDL).

DIFFERENTIAL — driver version, not code: workspace pnpm-lock.yaml pins `@tursodatabase/database: 0.7.1` (lines 11-13, 159-161, 310-312; resolution 2471); the live memory-server restarts cleanly on 0.7.1 with the identical index DDL (deploy pid 50088→88179, integrity ok). The adhd monorepo lock pins 0.7.2 (adhd pnpm-lock.yaml:1477) and crashes. Same DDL, different driver, different outcome → 0.7.2 regression.

FK issue (a): bookkeeping agent report (backlog_bookkeeping_implement_2026-08-08T19-30-00Z.json:40,103-104) documents '@tursodatabase/database-common native addon rejects FK references on UPDATE node when edge table has REFERENCES node(rowid) ON DELETE CASCADE — standard SQLite handles this' and records the workaround as a HAND-EDIT to /Users/nix/dev/node/adhd/node_modules/@adhd/sox-store-adapter/dist/turso-adapter.js:428 (`await this.db.exec('PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF')`) — a banned node_modules patch that (a) is absent from the workspace source (libs/data/store/store-adapter/src/turso-adapter.ts:716-778 _runTransaction has no such line) and (b) is silently wiped by any reinstall, leaving the CLI down again.

Workspace `libs/data/store/store-adapter` IS the source of the published `@adhd/sox-store-adapter` (npm latest 0.3.0; the dirty tree bumps it to an unpublished 0.4.0) and `libs/data/graph/graph-store` is the source of published `@adhd/sox-graph-store` (npm 0.7.0). The backlog CLI (adhd entrypoint/backlog, package.json deps `@adhd/sox-store-adapter: ^0.3.0`, `@adhd/sox-graph-store: ^0.6.0`) consumes both from npm — so sox-ecosystem IS the fix home for the published packages.
unverified: Why the backlog dist's single 'already exists' string (grep count 1) did not catch this error — the crash propagates uncaught; detail for the fixing agent
Whether the FK rejection (a) also reproduces on the workspace suite — it cannot, the workspace runs 0.7.1; the workspace's own memory-core writes edges with FK=ON (schema.ts:31) without issue
Whether a fixed driver exists upstream (0.7.3+/0.8.0-pre untested; 0.7.2 is latest stable)

files: sox-ecosystem: libs/data/store/store-adapter/package.json:28 (`@tursodatabase/database`: `^0.7.1` → `0.7.1` exact), extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/package.json:25, package.json:58 (root) — pin so the published adapter can never float to 0.7.2; relock (lock already 0.7.1) and commit the lock diff

adhd (separate repo, ops): relock @tursodatabase/database to 0.7.1 in /Users/nix/dev/node/adhd (pnpm-lock.yaml:1477 currently 0.7.2) via `pnpm add -w @tursodatabase/database@0.7.1` or pnpm.overrides; reinstall wipes the node_modules FK hand-edit; commit separately — adhd main is dirty with the in-flight better-sqlite3→Turso swap (entrypoint/backlog/package.json devDeps edit) and must not be stomped
functions: None in adapter source — under the 0.7.1 pin neither incompatibility needs adapter code; the FK workaround becomes unnecessary and must NOT be ported into the workspace source (it silently disables FK enforcement and would break memory-core's ON DELETE CASCADE semantics)
fixSurface.shape: Dependency pin (package.json x3 + lock) in sox-ecosystem + lock-only relock in adhd. Optionally harden graph-store/memory-core open path with a defensive catch of the 'already exists' parse error for index DDL (defense-in-depth for when the driver is eventually upgraded) — defer to a follow-up.
fixSurface.deferred: File the driver regression (upstream Turso + repo backlog item): 0.7.2 breaks CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS and FK-on-UPDATE; revisit 0.7.3+/0.8.0 when available.

blocks: plan-status.mjs --check (pre-commit hook gate, .husky/pre-commit runs `node tools/plan-status.mjs --check` unconditionally) — currently fails at the graph-read layer
Item 3's drift verification (cannot distinguish real drift from CLI crash until the CLI works)
Every future commit in sox-ecosystem that touches the pre-commit gate (the deploy already had to --no-verify, 3e9a40c0)

testPlan.name: TursoAdapter reopen-reapply schema must not throw under the locked driver (TURSO-DRIVER-072 guard)
testPlan.assertion: With @tursodatabase/database at 0.7.1: open a real Turso DB, apply the graph schema (unique indexes), close, reopen, re-apply the same DDL → no throw (0.7.1 honors IF NOT EXISTS). Executor proves red by temporarily resolving 0.7.2 in a scratch install: the same reopen-reapply throws 'Parse error: index node_uid_unique already exists' (BL-225 red leg), then restores 0.7.1 for green. Ops gate (live, equivalent weight): `backlog list-items --filter '{}'` is RED today (crash) and must be GREEN after the adhd relock; then `node tools/plan-status.mjs --check` exits 0 (or lists genuine drift, no crash).
testPlan.whyCatches: The guard asserts the property the 0.7.2 regression broke (schema re-apply idempotence on reopen); the workspace suite is the tripwire that catches any future driver float because the manifest currently allows it (`^0.7.1`).

packet.recommendation: Code+ops packet: (1) sox-ecosystem — pin driver 0.7.1 in 3 manifests + relock, commit by pathspec; (2) adhd — relock driver 0.7.1, reinstall (removes the node_modules hand-edit), commit separately without touching the in-flight swap; (3) verify backlog CLI + plan-status --check; (4) file the upstream driver regression. HIGH urgency — the backlog graph is currently unreachable by every CLI/MCP consumer.

items.title: PLAN/STATE 'drift' + ~30-file dirty main tree from an aborted changeset version run — real-drift question, reconciliation, and the misdiagnosed pre-commit failure
items.status: two causes separated; reconciliation packet defined; drift magnitude unverifiable until TURSO-DRIVER-072 lands

evidence: CAUSE 1 — the pre-commit failure is a BROKEN GRAPH READ, not provable drift: `node tools/plan-status.mjs --check` fails at tools/plan-status.mjs:137 with 'backlog list-items failed (exit 1)' because the backlog CLI crashes (item TURSO-DRIVER-072). plan-status's readGraphStatuses throws LOUDLY by design (D3: never swallow into an empty Map). The deploy report's attribution 'plan-status.mjs --check exit 1 due to PLAN.md/STATE.md drift from backlog graph (pre-existing)' is a misdiagnosis of the CLI crash — the check never reached the comparison stage.

Real drift ALSO almost certainly exists but is unverifiable until the CLI works: STATE.md derived block was last regenerated ~2026-08-05T19:12Z (STATE.md header), while the graph moved after — bookkeeping resolved PERF-MEMORY-004 / BUG-MEMORY-008 / BL-496 at 2026-08-09T01:08Z (bookkeeping report:44-69). `git status` shows docs/reporting/memory/ is CLEAN vs HEAD → no regeneration since those transitions.

CAUSE 2 — dirty tree = aborted `changeset version` run, ready but uncommitted AND unpublished: 5 consumed .changeset deletions (bug-memory-001-turso-error-classification.md, bug-memory-003-recall-kind-filter.md, conn-recycle-sox-store-adapter.md, embed-warmup-cachehit-retry.md, memory-invalidate-wrong-kind-idempotent.md — all tracked in HEAD), version bumps (memory-core 0.6.0→0.7.0, store-adapter 0.3.0→0.4.0, embedding-provider→0.3.0, + analysis/task-queue/hybrid-search/blob-store/vector-store/claim-verification), CHANGELOG entries, pnpm-lock.yaml. npm confirms NOTHING was published: @adhd/sox-memory-core latest 0.6.0, @adhd/sox-store-adapter latest 0.3.0.

The described code IS committed in HEAD (conn-recycle logic present in workspace turso-adapter.ts:690-778; memory-core changes landed in 41f241ef/cd9fcc65/d5836a49) — so the release is real and ready; reverting the .changeset deletions would resurrect already-consumed changesets. Repo convention for this exact state is a `chore(release):` commit (git log: b13b1278 'prepare 0.6.0 train, 18 packages', 8eb63727, c84e0af7).
registry/index.json at HEAD 3e9a40c0 is stamped provisional:true / builtFromCommit:+dirty (deploy report:134) — needs a clean restamp after the tree is clean.

SEPARATE OWNERSHIP in the dirty tree: docs/research/content-first/proxy/* (research scratch — cf-proxy/cf-rewrite/fj-proxy experiments + deleted .jsonl logs, NOT changeset artifacts), untracked extensions/agents/researcher/, tools/mcp-shell/, .opencode/research-trace/*, and 4 new .opencode/artifacts/reports/*.json (report files ARE tracked by convention — 34 already committed).

items.title: Live measurement packet: thin post-deploy data (write n=2, cluster 0 samples, embed p50 861ms cold) — what to collect after ~24h, how to prove a calibrated full enrich pass, acceptance numbers for the <600ms write→clustered-recall budget
items.status: protocol defined; acceptance criteria defined; no code changes required

evidence: Deploy report measurements (deploy_memory_perf_implement_2026-08-09T01-22-00Z.json:45-92): write_latency_ms post_deploy n=2 [68,157] vs baseline p50 919ms (n=11); cluster_pipeline declared (stages_declared 2→3, BL-496 instrument) with 0 samples — 'no cluster pass has run on the new backend'; embed p50 861ms cold over 7 samples (range 488-1660) vs ~330ms expected warm baseline

Telemetry is durable JSONL: ~/.adhd/sox-ecosystem/memory/logs/memory-core-<UTC-date>.jsonl (+ memory-server.live-service-*.jsonl), 5 required fields per record, trace-id threaded (docs/observability/README.md §1,§3)

Enrich tick lifecycle is durably instrumented: enrich.tick.* / enrich.pass.* events in the memory-core JSONL (STATE.md:381-384, BL-413 follow-on d016b63 — 'the 22.5h blind window is closed'); full-pass timeout budget SOX_ENRICH_FULL_TIMEOUT_MS=600s vs incremental 120s (STATE.md:385-387)

Periodic enrich is ON: SOX_DISABLE_PERIODIC_ENRICH removed per STATE.md S6 and confirmed absent from the live plist (deploy report:108). Manual full pass is safe: the previous live recluster completed in 74.4s (well under the 600s budget) with 440 communities/3596 members/72.5% coverage (STATE.md:388); deploy state was healthy (integrity ok, WAL 0 bytes, embed real/coreml, embeds_failed 0)

memory_ping exposes cluster_pipeline with paths full/incremental/subset and time_to_community_ms (BL-496, bookkeeping report:62-67); memory_stats exposes embed_provenance, cluster_count, coverage (deploy report:99-105)
unverified: Whether a manual full-enrich trigger exists (CLI/API on memory-server) or the periodic tick must be waited for — executing agent discovers in libs/memory-core/src during the run
Actual enrich tick interval (discover from enrich.tick.* event timestamps in JSONL)
Whether any recall traffic exists on the live server to exercise the recall side of the budget

fixSurface.shape: No code — a measurement protocol for a follow-up agent (performance or implement with measurement mandate). Collect after ~24h of runtime (from 2026-08-09T01:20Z deploy → ~2026-08-10T01:20Z): (1) memory_ping + memory_stats in-session; (2) jq over the JSONL: write.phaseA.finish duration_ms (n must grow well past 2 — target ≥30), embed.finish duration_ms p50/p95 warm, enrich.tick.*/enrich.pass.* presence + duration_ms + time_to_community_ms, tick_seq progression; (3) before/after cluster_count + coverage for the pass that ran. Guard proving a full pass ran UNDER CALIBRATION: an enrich.pass.full (cluster:full) event carrying duration_ms + time_to_community_ms, stages_declared=3, cluster_pipeline full/incremental/subset each >0 samples, and cluster_count/coverage recorded before+after.

blockedBy: P3 plan-status regeneration (do it before or after the 24h window, not during, to keep the measurement window clean)
dependencies.ordering: Runs after the ~24h soak; independent of P2 for the telemetry itself, but P2-first keeps the tree/commit flow sane while the window is open.

testPlan.name: Acceptance numbers to close the <600ms write→clustered-recall budget question
testPlan.assertion: 1) write_latency_ms p50 over n≥30 ≤ 600ms (expect ~100-200ms; 919ms baseline already smashed by 68/157ms); 2) embed p50 warm settles ≤ ~400ms (861ms cold must converge toward the ~330ms baseline) with embed backlog 0; 3) ≥1 enrich.pass.full inside the 24h window with time_to_community_ms p50 + p95 recorded; 4) composite: p95(write.phaseA.finish) + p50(time_to_community) ≤ 600ms — the write→clustered-recall budget. If recall traffic exists, also record recall latency; if not, state 'recall side unexercised' explicitly.
testPlan.whyCatches: The deploy explicitly declared these numbers unmeasurable at t+2min (cluster 0 samples, write n=2); this gate converts 'declared but unmeasured' into measured pass/fail and closes the PERF-MEMORY-004/BL-496 budget question with the exact events the instrumentation was built to emit.

packet.recommendation: Ops/measurement packet (no code): schedule ~24h after 2026-08-09T01:20Z; manual full enrich pass is safe now and recommended if the periodic tick has not fired a full pass by then (previous recluster 74.4s < 600s budget; state healthy); record before/after cluster_count/coverage; write the findings into the memory reporting tree (docs/reporting/memory/STATE.md) per the routing rules — not a parallel doc tree.
